facts.text: I have pain in my knee.
It's on the inner side of my shin bone, just below the kneecap.
It has been steadily getting worse.
I think it might be from volleyball. I've been playing recently, and it involves a lot of repetitive pivoting and twisting.
I recently joined a volleyball team, so I've been more physically active.
I've been trying to lose weight.

facts.item: trying to lose weight: medical advice
facts.text: At my last physical exam, I was told that losing weight could be good for my health.
I take birth control pills to manage my PCOS.
I haven't had any recent injuries.
I've never had anything like this before.

findings.name: knee examination
findings.result: Inspection: no visible abnormality, erythema or swelling; palpation: tenderness over the medial aspect of the tibia just below the patella; range of motion: full, without significant pain or limitation.

findings.name: knee X-ray
findings.result: No fracture, dislocation or appreciable joint effusion.

notes: Volleyball appears three times (History as the suspected cause, 'Increased physical activity', 'Has recently joined a volleyball team'): the patient's attribution is a context child of the knee pain (f005); the activity itself is one habit fact (f006).
'Recent weight loss attempt' (f007) and the advice at her last physical (f008, child) are kept apart: one is what she does, the other why.

The knee inspection, palpation and range of motion form one knee-examination record; the unnamed ligamentous instability tests are one special-test record. Obesity and hirsutism stay in the general-appearance exam record and are not patient facts.
The MRI leaf is excluded (no result; the source calls the MRI optional).
